issues.reason: The very rule cited reserves a bare `(Member <group> <prop>)` for "a property genuinely of the collection itself", and "international" is exactly such a non-distributing property — a workforce drawn from many countries — so distributing it would assert of each individual rescue worker something the text does not state, whereas the group-level atom is true and well-typed.

gaps_confirmed: A proper noun used as a modifier inside a common-noun compound ("Silk Road city"): the naming rules demand a symbol plus a mandatory `Name` for the proper noun while the compound rules bury an unexposed modifier in the fused symbol, so `silk_road_city` leaves "Silk Road" with no `Name`.

Whether a counted plural in OBJECT position ("killed more than 20,000 people") takes the per-member distribution rule — the distributive-predicate rule is stated subject-side and gives no guidance for a group filling `Patient`.
new_gaps: A collection-level adjective on a plural ("international rescue workers"): the plural rule names only size and name as properties of the collection, giving no test for adjectives that cannot distribute to members.

A possessive genitive whose possessed is a PLACE ("Iran's ... city of Bam"): the genitive's part/whole test routes to `PartOf` / `Possession`, while the geography rule bars `PartOf` for a place inside a place — nothing names `LocatedIn` as the genitive's output.
notes: The single filed issue applies the distributive half of the plural rule to a property that falls under its stated collection-level exception. The rest of the parse — `CardinalityAtLeast 20001`, the swapped `Before`, participial adjectives, and the inanimate transitive `Agent` — is per spec.
